notes:
A CORRECTION, NOT A NEW ADJUDICATION. bmdb 1541 hostap TP back-pass, group 1 of 5 (batches 1-2 rows, hostapd/config_file.c .. src/ap/pmksa_cache_auth.c). Batches 1-6 were labeled before Brandon's ADR-0011 rulings (aurora-lint bbf240e9, d9cb04d0). Checks made by every caller count (a function nothing outside the corpus can call, whose every call site explicitly tests the value, has a validated parameter), and every link of an argument's chain must end in a real proof. So each pointer-parameter TP row in those batches was re-checked for an FP basis under the full rule.

RESULT: 132 TP rows re-checked. 113 stay TP (each with a cited call site whose argument has no real proof) and 19 were proposed as FP. A fresh-context refuter upheld 18. It rejected src/ap/pmksa_cache_auth.c:52 (pmksa_cache_free_entry), whose file is built into the installed shared library libpasn.so, so its caller set is open; that row stays TP. The 18 flips: two function pointers each assigned exactly once whose every invocation passes a tested value (config_read_cb, the MLD ctrl-iface deinit pointer); six ctrl_iface cmd parameters passed buf + N from static hostapd_ctrl_iface_receive_process, whose 3 callers pass a local array or a tested pointer; &interfaces and &elems of locals; and explicit caller tests (sta, reply, buf, hapd, info in a while (info = dl_list_first(...)) loop). Only the 18 flipped rows change; the other 113 are untouched.

Mechanics follow bmdb 1490/1531 and the 1541 pilot: in-place edits keep each key; task-644-full-reaudit takes a row_count decrement and a superseded_rows record.

Counting basis: distinct (project, commit, file, line, rule) keys. No precision claim is made here.
